A smooth connected projective complex curve C of genus 21 has a line bundle L of degree 10, a fixed isomorphism L^4=K_C, a reduced six-point divisor Z, and basis r=xi*u of H0(C,L) with simple common divisor Z. Assume every hypothesis of prop:curve-data and prop:residue-data in the staged September-23-2026 manuscript, including evaluation surjectivity for all powers L^k with k>=3. In compatible coordinates at q_j, m_j=c_j/z_j with c_j nonzero, R_j=m_j*r and p_j=P-m_j*r' are holomorphic, P is a global meromorphic L^2 row with only the stated simple poles, p_j(0) wedge R_j(0)=1, and sum_j(R_j(0) wedge R_j'(0)-1)=-90. The rows r'(q_j) span C^2.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 048 ('A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf', unformalized in Lean), which claims to construct a characteristic-zero normal affine surface A with Der_C(A) ~= A^2 and a non-regular point (disproving the 1965 Lipman-Zariski conjecture): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/trace error, jet obstruction, or counterexample to one of the manuscript's intermediate lemmas (in 02-curve.tex, 03-trace.tex, 04-jets.tex, 05-analytic.tex, or 06-algebraization.tex) with a deterministic symbolic/computational refutation certificate, or (b) independently verify and strengthen the key algebraic/trace/jet identities with an exact machine-checkable certificate and primary-source citation audit.
There exists a finitely generated normal integral C-algebra A of dimension two with Der_C(A) isomorphic to A^2 and a nonregular localization at a maximal ideal.

In a nondegenerate complex quadratic plane, six nonzero vectors using three distinct nonisotropic directions twice, equal within each pair and avoiding any prescribed finite directions, can satisfy w=sum(w_j), Q(w)=90 and Q(w_j)+w_j dot w=1.

For the constructed fourth-contact curve, H0(Sigma,A_j) identifies with H0(C,K_C-jH) and surjects onto H0(Gamma,N_j), for j=0,...,3. Length-ell evaluations on C and Gamma agree for ell<=4; the four tabulated ranks are 6,12,12,10.

The construction yields smooth connected C of genus 21, reduced Z of degree 6, deg H=4, deg L=10, L=H+Z, theta=2L, normalized K_C=4L; a degree-four pencil unramified at Z with nonconstant marked values; h0(jH)=j+1 (0<=j<=3), h0(L)=h0(H+2Z)=2, h0(theta)=3, h0(O(Z))=1, h0(theta+H)=6, the stated multiplication identifications, and surjective evaluation H0((k+1)L)->H0(Z,(k+1)L|Z) for every k>=2, together with the elliptic quadratic data and vectors.

For f:C->P1 and Lambda=2L+H, f_*Lambda has the perfect symmetric trace form Tr(T1*T2/eta_C), splitting (3,0,0,-3), radical xi^2 H0(3H) on global sections and a nondegenerate two-dimensional quotient W. Local coefficient evaluation has dual square E(q)/s(q) at each q in Z.

Full double-pole principal parts induce an isomorphism iota:W->H0(Gamma,Phi) that identifies projective evaluations and whose dual is an isometry for the normalized quadratic form Q and the dual trace form.

For the constructed curve and six vectors there are c_j!=0 and a global P in H0(C,L^2(Z))^2 with principal part R_j(0)/z_j, where m_j=c_j/z_j, R_j=m_j r and p_j=P-m_j r' are holomorphic, p_j(0) wedge R_j(0)=1, W_j=R_j(0) wedge R_j'(0)=(v_j*)^2, and sum(W_j-1)=-9 deg L. Also J=u wedge P has trace pairing <[J],[T]>=-sum(c_j l_j(T)), unchanged by adding holomorphic L^2 pairs to P, and the pole prescription is compatible with fourth-root coordinates.

For D=t^k(b E_t+h d_z) and V=t^(ell+1)(A E_t+B d_z), [D,V] has the coefficients displayed in jets:general-bracket; div_sigma(D)=t^k((k-4)b+h'). The leading action is delta A_k=(1-k)br+hr', delta B_k=-khr.

Under the exact curve and residue hypotheses, after determinant-normalized horizontal matching by volume-preserving order-one and order-two flows, all four duality tests for the order-two vertical class in H1(C,L^3)^2 vanish.

For the data of prop:curve-data and prop:residue-data, finite compositions of holomorphic overlap flows of orders 1,...,7 fix C and its conormal L and admit rows A_k,B_k for 0<=k<=7 matching through index seven with A wedge B=t^2(1+O(t)). On a realization they give sections of I F/I^9 F with leading determinant t^4 E_t wedge d_z=t^5 d_t wedge d_z.

After shrinking, the finite overlap germs of prop:jets realize a smooth Hausdorff surface neighborhood Y of C with conormal L, C^2=-10, two sections of F/I^9 F and the prescribed logarithmic and ordinary determinant leading terms.
For n>=9, H1(C,F|C tensor L^n)=0; for E=I^9 F and every r>=1, H1(Y,E/I^r E)=0.
After shrinking Y about C, the quotient sections lift to holomorphic sections of F forming a frame of T_(Y minus C).

There is a normal complex surface germ with an isolated singular point and free analytic tangent sheaf of rank two, admitting a resolution whose exceptional set is a smooth genus-21 curve of self-intersection -10.
The manuscript's constructed germ has trivial dualizing sheaf, discrepancy -5 and p_g>=33, with p_g-g-b>=12. This is a remark, not an independently verified theorem.

For P=C[[x_1,...,x_e]], I=(f), a full syzygy presentation D and finite-length T1=ker(R^s->R^t)/sum R partial_j f, sufficiently high-order compatible approximations g,B with gB=0 are formally contact-equivalent: f=Phi(g)U, with Phi identity mod n^2 and U identity mod n.

Every normal isolated complex analytic germ of dimension d>=1 with free tangent module of rank d admits a finitely generated normal integral C-algebra A and closed point p with the same completed local ring, Der_C(A)=A^d, smooth complement of p, and nonregular A_p whenever the original germ is singular.
The smooth locus of the affine surface in thm:main has logarithmic Kodaira dimension two.
Iterated blowups of the surface in thm:main at its derivation module, with or without normalization, remain isomorphic to the original singular surface.
Serre duality on a smooth connected compact complex curve identifies H1(C,B) with H0(C,K_C tensor B^-1)^*, with overlap classes evaluated by the sum of positively oriented contour residues.
On each Stein chart and overlap, coherent analytic sheaves have zero positive cohomology (Cartan B); the resulting acyclic cover computes the first cohomology used in the Cousin splittings.

A meromorphic differential on a compact complex curve has total residue zero; Stokes' theorem gives the corresponding contour identity on a punctured curve and zero contour integral for dh with h single-valued holomorphic on an annulus.

A holomorphic vector field vanishing along a divisor has a time-one holomorphic flow germ, with inverse, after restricting transversely over a compact subannulus; finite compositions realize their Taylor series.
